title: Tool Schema Design — Naming, Descriptions, Parameter Constraints

questions.question: A model often chooses the wrong tool when several registry descriptions say look up information. What should the designer improve first?
options: Hide the entire registry until after the model answers
Make each name and description distinguish its intended use
Remove all usage guidance and keep short labels
Add more general tools with overlapping names
questions.explanation: When descriptions overlap, tool selection becomes ambiguous because the model cannot tell which boundary matches the request. Give each tool a stable name and distinct use condition; adding more overlapping names makes the same classification problem worse.

questions.question: Which description follows the lesson's recommended pattern?
options: Use whenever it seems useful and return some weather information.
This tool gets things, including weather, places, and other data.
Use when the user asks for current weather. Do not use for forecasts.
Weather data is available through this convenient helper.
questions.explanation: A useful description names a positive trigger and a close exclusion: current weather is in scope, forecasts are not. “Use whenever it seems useful” leaves the model no boundary between this tool and a forecast or general-information tool.

questions.question: Which tool name best follows the lesson's naming rules for retrieving weather?
options: get_weather_in_tokyo
get_weather
weather_get
get_weather_later
questions.explanation: `get_weather` is a stable snake_case verb-noun name and leaves the city in the arguments, so it works across locations. `get_weather_in_tokyo` hard-codes one parameter value, while `weather_get` reverses the preferred verb-noun order.

questions.question: A parameter accepts only Celsius or Fahrenheit. Which schema design best communicates that closed set?
options: A number field with a minimum and maximum
A string field with an enum listing the two values
An untyped object that accepts any nested value
A free-form string without a description
questions.explanation: An enum closes the string field to exactly Celsius or Fahrenheit, so generation and validation share the same allowed values. A free-form string permits unsupported labels such as “kelvin”; a numeric range cannot encode these names.

questions.question: A single tool has an action field with five possible operations. What rule of thumb applies?
options: Use a different generic tool name for every user
Rename the action field to command and remove its type
Split it into atomic tools with one clear action each
Keep one tool and pass the operation in a free-text field
questions.explanation: With five actions, a monolithic string forces the model to infer both the operation and its parameter shape. Split it into atomic typed tools; passing a free-text command preserves the ambiguity the schema is meant to remove.

questions.question: A tool executor rejects a missing city field. Which error message best helps the model recover?
options: TypeError: object of type NoneType has no attribute lower
Please try again with another prompt and see what happens
Invalid input: city is required. Example: {"city":"Bengaluru"}.
The request has failed due to an unknown exception
questions.explanation: A useful error names the missing city and shows a valid object, teaching the model how to repair the call. A raw TypeError exposes the executor’s implementation failure but neither identifies the required field nor supplies the expected shape.
